overview: Three 1946 documents cover Yomiuri correspondent Kitamura's request to move his family from Stockholm to Zurich, cleared by occupation intelligence and SCAP, with visa and frozen-fund details.

people.name: Hiroshi Kitamura
people.role: Yomiuri Shimbun foreign correspondent in Stockholm, seeking to continue as correspondent in Zurich

people.name: Kori Tanaka
people.role: Foreign Editor of the Yomiuri Shimbun

people.name: Yoshimura
people.role: Person prepared to negotiate with Swiss financial authorities for the release of living expenses from frozen funds

people.name: S. Iguchi
people.role: Director of General Affairs, Central Liaison Office

people.name: J. W. Burnett
people.role: Apparent drafter or preparing official of the United States Political Adviser’s office

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 415 on Hiroshi Kitamura’s proposed travel to Zurich
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The Political Adviser requests State Department guidance on allowing Yomiuri correspondent Hiroshi Kitamura and his family to move from Stockholm to Zurich.
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwards Kitamura's Zurich relocation request, noting no objection from G-2 or SCAP, and asks State's view.
keywords: United States Political Adviser for Japan

subfiles.title: Radiogram from Kitamura requesting transfer to Zurich
subfiles.to: Kori Tanaka and the Yomiuri Shimbun head office, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Kitamura asks the Yomiuri office to approve his transfer to Zurich so that he can continue working as a correspondent.
subfiles.summary: Kitamura asks Yomiuri's approval for his Zurich move, already holding a Swiss visa and seeking frozen-fund release.

subfiles.title: Central Liaison Office request for permission for the Kitamura family to enter Switzerland
subfiles.from: Central Liaison Office, Imperial Japanese Government
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The Japanese Government formally requests permission for Hiroshi Kitamura and his family to leave Sweden for Switzerland.
subfiles.summary: Japan's Central Liaison Office seeks permission for Kitamura's family to join him in Zurich, with visas already issued.

interest: Shows 1946 negotiations to move a Japanese correspondent's family from Stockholm to Zurich, across several authorities.
